title: Titan Pipeline
description: Titan YAML pipeline definition (design/29 §3). The pipeline body is accepted in either shape: at the document root (the canonical form) or nested under a top-level 'titan:' key (the legacy wrapper, kept for back-compat). This schema is the editor/tooling contract; TitanYamlParser is the runtime enforcer of the same contract.

oneOf.description: Canonical form — the pipeline body at the document root.
Legacy wrapper form — the pipeline body nested under 'titan:'.

agent.description: Default agent label for the whole pipeline. Optional. A stage with no 'agent' of its own inherits this; if neither is set, the work runs on any available agent.

failurePolicy.description: What the engine does when a node fails. 'blockOnFailure' (default) skips every non-terminal node on the first failure; 'continueOnFailure' lets the DAG run past a failure (only the dependent subgraph is cut).

libraries.description: Shared libraries to load for this pipeline. A map of <alias>: <coordinate-or-{url,credential}> (design/53). Each alias drives the `<alias>.<method>` dotted-step dispatch.

triggers.description: Schedules that start a build automatically (design/50). Each entry is a trigger — either a 'cron:' schedule or a 'github:' webhook (issue #397). Exactly one discriminator key per entry.

credentials.description: Stored credentials bound into every step of every stage (design/42). Flattened onto each step at parse time; stage- and step-level 'credentials' are appended after these, so precedence is step > stage > pipeline.

env.description: Environment variables injected into every step of every stage (GH #239). Stage- and step-level 'env' override these (step > stage > pipeline precedence). Values must be strings.

timeout.description: Pipeline-level execution deadline (issue #244). The outermost safety net: if no step- or stage-level 'timeout:' fires, the controller reaps the build at this deadline and marks it FAILED. Grammar: '30s', '5m', '2h', '1d', or a bare number of seconds.

notify.description: Lifecycle hooks fired by the orchestrator at the build's terminal state (#245), regardless of which step ran. Each entry is a webhook (today) or slack (future) sink; auth tokens MUST travel via 'credentialsId', never inline in 'url'.

concurrency.description: Per-job concurrency limit (#1101). Caps the number of RUNNING builds of this job; new builds either queue, cancel the oldest RUNNING build, or cancel other QUEUED builds, per 'on_overflow'. Absent: unlimited (legacy default).

priority.description: Per-job queue priority (#1100). Discriminated-union string — one of 'high' (10), 'normal' (0, default), or 'low' (-10). Builds of higher-priority jobs are claimed from task_queue before lower-priority ones; same-priority builds preserve FIFO. Bare integers are rejected by design — use the named tier.

buildRetention.description: Per-job build-history retention override (#640). Caps this job's titan.builds rows at the last 'keepLast' entries; older builds (and their flow_nodes / artifact / test_result / task_queue / logs / task_archive rows) are dropped by the daily prune. When absent, the server-wide TITAN_JOB_BUILD_RETENTION default applies. 'keepLast: 0' is the per-job opt-out — keeps full history regardless of the global default.

include.description: Pipeline fragments to inline before parsing (issue #1120). Each entry is either a repo-relative path string (sibling YAML fragment) or an object { repo, ref, path[, credential] } for a cross-repo fragment. Includes are resolved depth-first with cycle detection; list keys (stages, parameters, triggers, notify, credentials) are concatenated with the main file's, map keys (libraries, env) are shallow-merged with the main file winning, and all other keys are overridden by the main file.

stages.description: The pipeline DAG: stage, gate and precondition nodes. Order of this list does not imply order of execution — 'dependsOn' does. Sibling nodes with the same 'dependsOn' run in parallel.

stringOrList.description: A single string, or a list of strings.

default.description: Default value when the build does not supply one.

required.description: Whether a value must be supplied.

choices.description: Allowed values for a choice parameter.

trigger.description: A build trigger — exactly one of a 'cron' schedule (design/50), a 'github' webhook (issue #397), a 'gitlab' webhook (issue #1078) or a 'bitbucket' webhook (issue #1079).

cron.description: A standard 5-field cron schedule (with 'H' for a hashed/jittered value), with the @daily/@hourly aliases and a 'TZ=' prefix all supported.

github.description: A GitHub webhook trigger (issue #397). Fires when a verified delivery from github.com arrives at /api/v1/triggers/github whose repository matches this job and whose branch matches one of the configured globs.

gitlab.description: A GitLab webhook trigger (issue #1078). Fires when a verified delivery from gitlab.com (or a self-hosted instance) arrives at /api/v1/triggers/gitlab whose X-Gitlab-Token matches the configured shared-secret credential and whose event kind / ref matches the configured filters.

bitbucket.description: A Bitbucket Cloud webhook trigger (issue #1079). Fires when a verified delivery from bitbucket.org arrives at /api/v1/triggers/bitbucket whose X-Hub-Signature HMAC matches the configured secret credential and whose event kind / ref matches the configured filters.

githubTrigger.description: A GitHub-webhook trigger value (issue #397) — the inner object under a `github:` discriminator on a trigger entry.

branches.description: Glob patterns the delivery's branch must match. Empty / omitted means any branch. Patterns follow Titan's glob convention — e.g. 'trunk', 'feat/**', 'release-*'.

events.description: GitHub event types this trigger accepts — 'push' and / or 'pull_request'. Defaults to ['push'].

credentialsId.description: The credentials-store id of the HMAC secret GitHub signs deliveries with. Resolved at receive time via CredentialsService — the plaintext secret is NEVER stored in the pipeline config.

gitlabTrigger.description: A GitLab-webhook trigger value (issue #1078) — the inner object under a `gitlab:` discriminator on a trigger entry.

branches.description: Glob patterns the delivery's ref must match. Empty / omitted means any ref. Applies to the branch name for push, the tag name for tag_push, and the source-branch name for merge_request.

events.description: GitLab event kinds this trigger accepts — any of 'push', 'merge_request', 'tag_push'. Defaults to ['push'].

credentialsId.description: The credentials-store id of the shared-secret token GitLab sends in X-Gitlab-Token. Resolved at receive time via CredentialsService — the plaintext token is NEVER stored in the pipeline config and NEVER logged.

bitbucketTrigger.description: A Bitbucket-webhook trigger value (issue #1079) — the inner object under a `bitbucket:` discriminator on a trigger entry.

branches.description: Glob patterns the delivery's ref must match. Empty / omitted means any ref. Applies to the pushed branch name for push and the source (head) branch for pull_request.

events.description: Bitbucket event kinds this trigger accepts — any of 'push', 'pull_request'. Defaults to ['push'].

credentialsId.description: The credentials-store id of the HMAC secret Bitbucket signs deliveries with (X-Hub-Signature). Resolved at receive time via CredentialsService — the plaintext secret is NEVER stored in the pipeline config and NEVER logged.

node.description: One DAG node: exactly one of a stage, a gate, or a precondition.

stage.description: A stage: a named group of steps.
Stage name (also the basis of its node id).

agent.description: Agent label for this stage's steps. Optional — omit it to inherit 'titan.agent'.

steps.description: The steps this stage runs, in order.

use.description: Stage-level local-template inlining (design/56). The template's step list replaces the stage's steps at parse time, with ${param.<name>} substituted from 'with'. Mutually exclusive with 'steps:', 'matrix:' and 'each:' on the same stage.

credentials.description: Stored credentials bound into every step of this stage (design/39). Flattened onto each step at parse time; a step's own 'credentials' are appended after these.

sshAgent.description: SSH-agent credential ids (each an SSHUserPrivateKey) loaded for every sh/script step of this stage (design/41). Flattened onto each step at parse time, de-duplicated; a step's own 'sshAgent' ids are appended after these.

image.description: Default container image for this stage's steps.

retry.description: Default retry policy for every step of this stage (design/44). Flattened onto each step at parse time; a step's own 'retry' wins.

timeout.description: Default execution deadline for every step of this stage (e.g. 30s, 5m, 2h). Flattened onto each step; a step's own 'timeout' wins.

when.description: Condition expression — the stage runs only if it evaluates true.

dependsOn.description: Node ids this stage waits for. Empty = runs immediately.

onFailure.description: Upstream stage names whose failure triggers this stage (design/68). When set, this stage is a failure handler: it advances iff at least one listed upstream reached FAILED, AND the optional 'when:' expression is true. Mutually exclusive with 'dependsOn:' on the same stage.

env.description: Environment variables injected into every step of this stage (GH #239). Each key must be a non-blank string; each value must be a string. Step-level env overrides stage-level; stage-level overrides pipeline-level.

matrix.description: Stage-level matrix (design/54). Cartesian product of named axes, optionally filtered by 'exclude' and augmented by 'include'. Fans the stage out into one stage per cell at parse time; step arguments may reference the cell with ${matrix.<axis>}.

each.description: Stage-level 1D iteration (design/55). Fans the stage out into one stage per element of 'in' at parse time; step arguments may reference the cell with ${each.<var>}. Mutually exclusive with 'matrix:' in v1.

notify.description: Lifecycle hooks fired by the orchestrator when this stage reaches its terminal state, regardless of which step ran (#245). Each entry is a webhook (today) or slack (future) sink; auth tokens MUST travel via 'credentialsId', never inline in 'url'.

gate.description: A gate: a pause point in the DAG, typically a human approval.

requiresApproval.description: Whether the gate needs a human approval to advance.

approvers.description: Users or groups allowed to approve.

dependsOn.description: Node ids this gate waits for.

precondition.description: A precondition: an expression that must hold for the DAG to proceed past it.

expression.description: Expression that must evaluate true for downstream nodes to run.

dependsOn.description: Node ids this precondition waits for.

step.description: A step: exactly one descriptor key (sh, script, checkout, …) — plus an optional 'image' for the container it runs in. The descriptor set is open (the StepHandler SPI is extensible); a few common ones are listed here for assistance.

credentials.description: Stored credentials bound into this step as masked, step-scoped environment (design/39 / D6). Resolved on the controller at dispatch; the worker never sees the credentials store.

sshAgent.description: SSH-agent credential ids (each an SSHUserPrivateKey) loaded into a per-step ssh-agent for the step's shell process (design/41). Valid on 'sh' and 'script' steps only; rejected on any other descriptor. Resolved on the controller at dispatch.

image.description: Container image this step runs in (overrides the stage 'image').

retry.description: Declarative per-step retry policy (design/44). Valid on any executable step. Absent = no retry; the controller re-enqueues a failed step's task with backoff up to maxAttempts.

timeout.description: Execution deadline for this step (e.g. 30s, 5m, 2h). When the step overruns it, the controller fails the node and the worker kills the process.

when.description: Condition guarding this step (GH #1093). Either a CEL string, or a structured block with exactly one of: branch (glob), previous (success|failure|always), files_changed (glob list). A false condition skips the step (status SKIPPED).

env.description: Environment variables injected into this step (GH #239). Merged with pipeline- and stage-level env at dispatch time (step > stage > pipeline precedence). Values must be strings.

sh.description: Run a shell command on the agent.

echo.description: Print a message to the build log.

checkout.description: Check out source for the build.

scriptStep.description: A 'script' step: a body of code run by a named runtime on the agent.

runtime.description: The runtime that executes the body.

credentialBinding.description: One credential binding (design/39 / design/32 D6): a credential-store id bound into the step as masked, step-scoped environment. Not a wrapping step — Titan has no blocks; a binding is a declarative property of the step.

usernameVariable.description: Env var bound to the username (usernamePassword, sshKey).

passwordVariable.description: Env var bound to the password (usernamePassword).

variable.description: Env var bound to the secret value (string) or the secret file's path (file).

keyFileVariable.description: Env var bound to the path of the materialised private-key file (sshKey).

passphraseVariable.description: Env var bound to the key passphrase (sshKey).

retryPolicy.description: A declarative per-step retry policy (design/44 §2) — a Temporal-shaped policy with bounded attempts, exponential backoff with a cap, and an optional retryable-exit-code allowlist. Two forms: an integer shorthand 'retry: N' (N attempts, default backoff), or the object form.

oneOf.description: Shorthand: total attempts including the first (1 = no retry), with the default backoff (initial 10s, multiplier 2.0, max 5m).

maxAttempts.description: Total attempts including the first; 1 = no retry.

backoff.description: The exponential-backoff schedule. The delay before retry k (1-indexed) is min(initial * multiplier^(k-1), max).

initial.description: Delay before the first retry — a duration suffixed s/m/h.

max.description: Cap on the computed delay — a duration suffixed s/m/h; must be >= initial.

retryableExitCodes.description: If set, retry only when the step's exit code is in this list; any other non-zero exit fails fast. If absent, any non-zero exit is retryable.

whenCondition.description: A structured step condition (GH #1093): a discriminated union — declare exactly one of branch, previous or files_changed. A false condition skips the step (SKIPPED).

branch.description: Run only when the build's branch matches this glob (e.g. 'main', 'release/*').

previous.description: Run based on the prior step's outcome: success (prior succeeded). NOTE: 'failure' and 'always' are [experimental] — under the engine's default fail-fast mode an upstream failure halts the build before a downstream step is dispatched, so a 'failure'/'always' guard does not yet fire in the upstream-failed scenario (the AncestorClosure fail-fast exemption is a tracked follow-up). 'success' and all parse/evaluation semantics are fully supported today.

files_changed.description: Run only when at least one changed file in the build matches one of these globs.

matrix.description: Stage-level matrix (design/54). A Cartesian product of named axes, optionally filtered by 'exclude' and augmented by 'include'. Fans the stage out into one stage per cell at parse time; step arguments may reference the cell with ${matrix.<axis>}.

axes.description: Named axes of the product. Order is preserved. Each axis is a non-empty list of scalar values (strings, numbers, booleans).

exclude.description: Cells (full or partial — every key matches) to drop from the Cartesian product.

include.description: Off-grid cells to add to the matrix after 'exclude'. Each entry must name every declared axis.

maxParallel.description: Cap on how many cells run concurrently. Carried onto every generated cell stage; engine-honoured at dispatch.

fail_fast.description: When true (default), any cell failure aborts the fan-out group. When false, every remaining cell runs to completion and the parent stage reports failure only after all cells finish. (#1092)

each.description: Stage-level 1D iteration (design/55). Fans the stage out into one stage per element of 'in' at parse time; step arguments may reference the cell with ${each.<var>}. Mutually exclusive with 'matrix:' in v1.

var.description: The binding name. Substitution syntax is ${each.<var>}. Must be a valid identifier and must not collide with a reserved name (each, matrix, env, params).

in.description: Non-empty list of scalar values to iterate over.

maxParallel.description: Cap on how many cells run concurrently. Carried onto every generated cell stage; engine-honoured at dispatch.

use.description: Stage-level local-template inlining (design/56). 'from' is a repo-relative path to a template file; 'with' supplies keyword args. The template's step list replaces the stage's steps at parse time, with ${param.<name>} substituted. Mutually exclusive with 'steps:', 'matrix:' and 'each:' on the same stage.

from.description: Relative local path to the template file, resolved against the pipeline file's directory. Traversal within the repo root is allowed; escaping the repo root is a parse error. Remote / git-ref'd reuse is the domain of 'libraries:' (design/53).

with.description: Keyword args passed to the template — each key must name a 'params:' entry declared by the template; values are typed-coerced where safe.

includeEntry.description: One include entry (#1120). Either a repo-relative path string to a sibling YAML fragment, or an object { repo, ref, path[, credential] } for a cross-repo fragment fetched via the controller's library fetcher.

oneOf.description: Local include: a repo-relative path to a sibling YAML fragment. URI schemes and absolute paths are rejected (use the object form for cross-repo).

repo.description: Git URL of the source repo (https://, ssh://, file://, ...).

ref.description: Tag, branch, or full commit SHA to fetch at.

path.description: Path inside the source repo to the YAML fragment.

credential.description: Optional secret-store id used to authenticate the fetch (design/40). Plaintext secrets MUST NOT appear here.

notifyHook.description: One lifecycle hook entry (#245). Fired by the orchestrator at the owning scope's terminal state, regardless of which step ran.

type.description: The hook kind. 'webhook' = plain HTTP POST (url required, credentialsId optional). 'slack' = Slack inbound-webhook (credentialsId REQUIRED — the stored secret is the workspace-token-bearing URL; url MUST NOT be inline — CONSTITUTION §6).

on.description: Terminal-state predicates this hook fires on. Empty means 'always'.

url.description: The POST target URL. Required for 'type: webhook'.

credentialsId.description: CredentialsService id resolved at dispatch time (design/39). Required for 'type: slack' (the stored secret is the workspace-token-bearing URL); optional for 'type: webhook' (auth header). NEVER store the literal secret here — this is an id reference (CONSTITUTION §6 — NO plaintext secret in config_json).

channel.description: Optional Slack channel override (e.g. '#deploys'). Plain display string, not a secret. Only valid for 'type: slack'.

buildRetention.description: Per-job build-retention override (#640). 'keepLast: N' caps this job's build history at the last N rows; 'keepLast: 0' keeps full history for this job regardless of the server-wide default.

keepLast.description: Maximum builds to retain for this job. 0 disables the prune for this job (keeps full history).

concurrency.description: Per-job concurrency limit (#1101). Caps the number of RUNNING builds of this job. Either an integer (short form) or {max, on_overflow}.

oneOf.description: Short form: maximum RUNNING builds of this job, >= 1.

max.description: Maximum RUNNING builds of this job, >= 1.

on_overflow.description: Behaviour when a new build arrives at the concurrency ceiling. 'queue' (default) holds the new build until the cap clears; 'cancel_oldest' SIGTERMs the oldest RUNNING build; 'cancel_pending' cancels other QUEUED builds of this job and lets the new build through.

priority.description: Per-job queue priority (#1100). One of: 'high' (weight 10), 'normal' (0, default), 'low' (-10). Higher-priority builds are claimed from task_queue first.
